You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a classic public goods game: keeping tokens is individually optimal since contributing only returns 0.3 per token to oneself versus keeping the full value, but if everyone contributed fully the group would be better off overall. I need to decide between the self-interested choice of contributing nothing versus the cooperative choice of contributing everything.

Without punishment mechanisms beyond withholding future contributions, conditional cooperation could still sustain some cooperation over repeated rounds. I'll start with a moderate contribution of 10 as an opening signal, then adapt based on how others respond.

With 10 rounds and no punishment mechanism, the rational move is to free-ride, so I'll contribute 0 and keep the full endowment private.
